overview: Two sequential events in early human development — sperm meeting egg, followed later by the resulting embryo attaching to the uterine wall.
genZNote: Fertilization: the meet-cute between sperm and egg. Implantation: the embryo finally moving in and settling down.

aspects.label: What Happens
aspects.valueA: Fusion of sperm and secondary oocyte to form a zygote.
aspects.valueB: Attachment and embedding of the blastocyst into the endometrial lining.

aspects.label: Location
aspects.valueA: Typically occurs in the ampulla of the fallopian tube.

aspects.label: Approximate Timing
aspects.valueA: Occurs within about 24 hours of ovulation.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Fertilisation happens in the fallopian tube, not the uterus — a very commonly tested location fact.
overlay.memoryTrick: Fertilization = the union. Implantation = the settling in, days later, in a different location.
overlay.commonMisconception: Pregnancy is not medically considered to have 'started' at fertilisation in most clinical definitions — implantation, several days later, is often used as the defining starting point.
